objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

## The measured rule, restated as the mechanism this round implements

Six mechanisms measured on the frozen baseline (Stage 2: 3000 epochs, four cards;
Stage 3: 150 epochs, width-20 beam, 57,439 rows) all land at or below the baseline's own
0.055537. The per-position forensics say why: they changed the *structure* of the SID
space, while Recall@10 is ordered by **coverage** (whether the target's complete SID is
among the twenty beams), and coverage is decided by the *semantic partition* -- which
items share a prefix with which other items. The arms that reach 0.062-0.064 have a
behaviourally coherent partition, not a different bucket statistic.

This round therefore implements the one class that was never tested on the baseline: a
**behaviour-cohesion term in the quantised code space**. The train-only directed successor
pairs (an item and an observed next target) are pulled into the same *assigned first-level
codeword*, so behaviour neighbours end up sharing a prefix, while the reconstruction loss
keeps the space alive. Nothing about the assignment geometry, the codebook capacity or the
Sinkhorn path changes, which is deliberate: every mechanism that perturbed them was
unstable or neutral in the measurements.

Requirements:

* the cohesion term must act on the *assigned codeword* of the first level, so its gradient
  reaches the codebook and, through the straight-through estimator, the encoder;
* the term must be scale-matched to the reconstruction loss (the code distance is O(1) and
  the reconstruction is ~1e-4), otherwise the encoder collapses within one epoch;
* behaviour-off must keep the number of pairs but destroy the item-successor relation
  (the successors are shuffled), and geometry-off must act on the raw encoder output
  instead of the assigned codeword, so the two ablations separate "behaviour" from
  "quantised geometry";
* the codebook capacity stays the baseline's (256, 256, 256): the coarse first level must
  come from the behaviour structure concentrating the *usage*, not from shrinking the
  codebook (a 32-code first level leaves the last level's residual distances constant and
  the Sinkhorn path refuses to train).

## Required measurement contract

State the predicted direction of: `L1 Hard ER` (canonical 52,855 pairs, ten fixed
negatives), gold-prefix survival at depths 1-4, teacher-forced top-1 accuracy of T1..T4, and
Stage 3 `test_R@10`. The reference to beat is 0.055537 (the baseline control, measured with
the identical frozen protocol) and the target is 0.065.

## Frozen constraints

Four tokens (three learned levels plus the deterministic collision-extension token), 3000
Stage 2 epochs on four cards, no early stopping, no test-time tuning, the frozen Stage 3
protocol, no validation or test behaviour in SID construction, and a one-epoch smoke close
to the baseline's cost.

findings.correction: Put an explicit curved operation (for example, map encoder vectors and trainable codewords to the Poincare ball and compute Poincare-distance-based assignment/cohesion) directly in the same successor-pair pathway; retain a true Euclidean geometry-off comparison and document safe curvature/projection bounds.
findings.detail: The implementation does not implement the stated behaviour × hyperbolic coupling. GEOMETRY_ON changes the cohesion representation between looked-up first-level code vectors and raw encoder outputs, not between curved and Euclidean geometry. VQLayer assignment and its distances remain Euclidean. The Poincare helpers in model/utils.py are not used by the trainer/model path. Thus this is not one connected behaviour-and-curvature computation.
findings.reproduction: Follow main's BEHAVIOUR_ON=True, GEOMETRY_ON=True path: _cohesion_term compares code vectors by squared Euclidean difference (train_rqvae.py:264-265); assignment uses the Euclidean squared-distance expression (model/layers.py:98-104). Replacing or removing model/utils.py's Poincare helpers cannot affect this execution. The declared GEOMETRY_ON=False branch merely switches codes to encoder(batch) (train_rqvae.py:396-398).

findings.correction: Make the behaviour-conditioned curved computation differentiable with respect to the intended encoder and codebook parameters (for example, a distance-based soft/straight-through assignment or a curved pairwise latent/code objective), then verify finite loss/gradients and behaviour-off plus Euclidean controls in the prescribed smoke.
findings.detail: The enabled cohesion term has no differentiable path to the encoder: latent is computed inside torch.no_grad at lines 391-392, then converted by hard argmin to indices and used only for embedding lookup at lines 393-395. The cohesion term can update the codebook embeddings, but cannot update encoder parameters through that branch. In addition, there is no curved-vs-Euclidean switch comparison because GEOMETRY_ON is not a geometry switch. The required coupled pathway's intended gradient/assignment effects therefore are not established.
findings.reproduction: With BEHAVIOUR_ON=True and GEOMETRY_ON=True, take loss.backward(): the cohesion contribution is constructed solely from embedding lookup vectors after the encoder forward was under no_grad, so its encoder gradient contribution is absent. Set GEOMETRY_ON=False and the term instead operates on encoder(batch), which does yield an encoder path, but this is not a curved-distance ablation. The ordinary reconstruction/quantization losses may still train; that does not repair this defect in the proposed term.

findings.correction: Restore the launcher's GENREC_SINGLE_GPU branch: when SINGLE_GPU_ENV is set, run the script as one process without spawning four workers; preserve the existing torchrun branch otherwise.
findings.detail: The launcher has only a fixed four-process torchrun path and no single-card branch consulting SINGLE_GPU_ENV="GENREC_SINGLE_GPU". This fails the explicitly required distributed-launcher compatibility. The visible paths otherwise resolve to the repository's frozen sentence_t5.npy and train.parquet (lines 64-67), candidate-named results/stage2_RQ-VAE/TIGER_behaviour_code_cohesion (lines 59-70), and the export assigns rows by enumerate(item_id) across all embedding rows (lines 491-504); no contrary path/index defect is evident from inspection.
findings.reproduction: Set GENREC_SINGLE_GPU in the environment and invoke the script directly: _launch_via_torchrun does not inspect it and still builds --nproc_per_node=4 with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 (lines 107-117, 515-530), rather than taking the single-card route.

findings.correction: Replace both `codes.device` references with a defined tensor device, e.g. `latent.device` (or `codewords.device`), and then run the required one-epoch gradient smoke to verify finite cohesion/reconstruction losses and gradients to encoder and codebook. The current defect prevents testing whether assignments/gradients change under behaviour-off and geometry-off controls.
findings.detail: _cohesion_term references `codes.device`, but no variable named `codes` exists in the function or module. Any batch with at least one valid successor pair reaches this line and raises NameError before producing the cohesion loss, so no real forward/backward or optimizer step can complete. The behaviour-on configuration creates exactly this case when a batch contains a transition endpoint pair.
findings.reproduction: Call _cohesion_term(latent, item_rows, np.array([[item_rows[0], item_rows[1]]]), codewords) with distinct valid item IDs and a non-empty batch; execution reaches `device=codes.device` and raises NameError. The trainer invokes this term every minibatch with BEHAVIOUR_ON=True and the loaded successor pairs.

findings.correction: Sample or deterministically select at most `COHESION_BATCH_PAIRS` pairs per minibatch and compute per-pair expected code distance directly (e.g. `(assignment[left] @ code_distance * assignment[right]).sum(-1).mean()`), avoiding the P-by-P matrix. Then confirm finite loss/gradients and behavior/geometry switch effects in the specified GPU smoke.
findings.detail: `assignment[left_rows] @ code_distance @ assignment[right_rows].t()` constructs a dense matrix quadratic in the number of valid successor pairs. `_successor_pairs` allows up to 200,000 pairs (line 227), so this can require tens of billions of entries and cannot run as intended; `COHESION_BATCH_PAIRS = 4096` is declared but never used to bound this computation. Thus finite trainable gradients for the configured real path cannot be established and the likely allocation failure blocks training.
findings.reproduction: Use 4096 or more valid behavior pairs in a minibatch: `pair_cost` has shape [P,P] (at P=4096, 16,777,216 elements; at the allowed 200,000, 40 billion elements) before taking its diagonal. The fixed pair limit permits the latter, and the batch-pair constant does not cap P.

findings.correction: Make the entry point invoke `main()` only when `_launch_via_torchrun()` indicates that it did not already run it (for example, have the launcher return a boolean), or make the single-card branch launch/return from the entry point so the unconditional second call cannot happen. Preserve the existing torchrun child behavior.
findings.detail: In the single-card branch, `_launch_via_torchrun()` calls `main()` when `GENREC_SINGLE_GPU` is set, returns, and then the module-level code calls `main()` again. A single-GPU invocation therefore runs the complete training/export twice sequentially instead of once.
findings.reproduction: Set `GENREC_SINGLE_GPU=1` and execute train_rqvae.py: `_launch_via_torchrun` enters lines 538-540 and completes main; control returns to line 563, which invokes main a second time. The second pass reinitializes and retrains, overwriting candidate outputs.

stage3_results.note: the mechanism did what it was designed to do -- the first level collapsed into 16 behaviour cohorts and the canonical positive-prefix rate rose from the baseline's 0.082 to 0.430 -- and Recall still did not improve over the baseline, which is the seventh mechanism to land at or below it
